description: The non-major branch, digests and pinned digests included, merges itself once its checks are green; lock file maintenance and security fixes too. Majors and Go toolchain minors keep the tick. Renovate merges on its own green read of the combined commit status, so no branch protection is required.

packageRules.description: Non-major updates share one branch and merge themselves once its checks are green. One grouped branch per run instead of one per dependency: every open branch costs a full CI run each time it is rebased, and a small runner pool cannot absorb twenty of them per push. The branch rebases when it falls behind, at most once per Renovate run.
With minor and patch combined, Renovate offers only the highest non-major Go version, a minor that waits for approval, so the toolchain patch would never be proposed. Go keeps them apart.

A Go toolchain minor decides what compiles the shipped binaries and raises the floor for contributors. It stays a deliberate, dashboard-approved change outside the group; toolchain patches still merge themselves. The tick is its gate, so it carries no soak: a tick on an update still inside its soak is discarded.
Go toolchain patches merge themselves in their own branch: kept apart from minors, they cannot share the non-major group's branch.
